learning_outcomes.description: Analyse foodservice management principles and systems and discuss the role of dietitians across diverse foodservice settings.

Develop, adapt and assess recipes and menus for diverse populations and settings, ensuring alignment with evidence-based nutrition standards or guidelines and incorporating nutritional, cultural, operational, consumer and sustainability considerations.
Critically evaluate and apply food safety and risk management frameworks to support regulatory, and organisational compliance.
Apply organisational management, financial management, human resources, change management and quality improvement principles and activities to support effective foodservice systems and operations.
Identify and explain opportunities for continuous quality improvement to enhance service delivery, consumer satisfaction, and organisational outcomes.

assessments.task_description:
Quiz 1 will cover workshop content from weeks 1-3. Quiz will be held at the start of Workshop 4.

Quiz 2 will cover workshop content from weeks 4-7. Quiz will be held at the start of Workshop 8.


Use of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Translation (MT) 

This assessment task is to be completed in-person. The use of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) or Machine Translation (MT) tools will not be permitted. Any attempted use of AI or MT may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct.
assessments.submission_guidelines: Students will complete a paper-based exam in class.
assessments.deferral_or_extension: You may be able to defer this exam.
assessments.late_submission: You will receive a mark of 0 if this assessment is submitted late.
assessments.additional_info: You may be able to defer this exam.

assessments.assessment_title: Integrated Menu Assessment and Foodservice Evaluation Report
assessments.task_description:
Students will be provided with a Residential Aged Care Home scenario in which they are required to complete an individual menu review and provide recommendations to enhance the foodservice system. Group activities completed in Workshop 3 will support students in completing the first steps of the menu review. See Blackboard for more details.

Use of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Translation (MT) 

This task has been designed to be challenging, authentic and complex. Whilst students may use AI and/or MT technologies, successful completion of assessment in this course will require students to critically engage in specific contexts and tasks for which artificial intelligence will provide only limited support and guidance.

A failure to reference generative AI or MT use may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct.

To pass this assessment, students will be required to demonstrate detailed comprehension of their written submission independent of AI and MT tools.
assessments.submission_guidelines: Submit via the relevant Turnitin submission portal on the course Blackboard site.
assessments.deferral_or_extension: You may be able to apply for an extension.
assessments.late_submission: A penalty of 10% of the maximum possible mark will be deducted per 24 hours from time submission is due for up to 7 days. After 7 days, you will receive a mark of 0.
assessments.additional_info: You may be able to apply for an extension.
